title: Slate Compressor: initial scoping and prioritization for high-touch account asks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Sales and CS funnel an asynchronous flood of feature asks from high-touch enterprise prospects. Current first-pass triage is slow, inconsistent, and produces large, disparate tickets that burden PM and Eng review cycles. Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable 'Slate Compressor' intake flow that aggregates related asks into prioritized "slates" for rapid economic sizing and decisioning. Outcomes: (1) ~40% reduction in initial review volume for PMs, (2) consistent trade-off frames (cost/latency/risk/regulatory), (3) fast handoff docs for Solutions/Eng to scope and estimate.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming enterprise asks are bucketed into a Slate within 48 hours of CS submission
Each Slate has a canonical one-paragraph problem statement, 3 prioritized solution options, and a first-pass econ delta (low/med/high)
PM lead can decide Go/No-Go for implementation vs pilot vs nurture within one cycle
Templates and playbook are documented and used by at least two CS teams as measured by intake form adoption
tasks: Draft Slate Compressor intake form (fields: account, ask cluster tags, business outcome, rough econ, compliance constraints, urgency)
Prototype a weekly auto-aggregation job that groups asks by overlapping customer intents and product area (PoC: CSV + manual rules)
Design 1-pager Slate template for PM/Eng handoff
Run 2 pilot clusters with Sales East and Strategic CS to validate signal grouping and field coverage
Create internal playbook (Confluence) with decision matrix and rollup examples
decisions: Use business-impact-first prioritization: rank by ARR/strategic importance, technical effort estimate, and compliance risk
Keep initial aggregation rules simple (keyword + product-area mapping) and avoid ML-based clustering in Phase 1
Ship a manual semi-automated workflow for now; revisit automation after 4 pilot slates

Implement semi-automated aggregator (script + owner mapping) and run first weekly cluster job (owner: Marco) — schedule 2025-01-20

risks: Over-aggregation: merging unrelated asks could hide edge regulatory requirements
Under-aggregation: leaving too many small slates won’t reduce PM load
Automation early: premature ML clustering could introduce opaque grouping and damage trust with CS
Resource contention: Eng estimates may slip if multiple slates hit same subsystem simultaneously
notes: Pilot metrics to capture: time-to-first-review, slate-to-decision time, % of slates routed to pilot vs backlog, sample econ delta accuracy
When scaling, consider integration with Redwood Console to tag slates by model/route impact (latency/cost annotations)
If a slate has a deployment constraint of 'on-prem' or 'air-gapped', escalate to Security & Compliance review and flag as high implementation cost
